tinyblocks.guide.page.1:
§lTinyBlocks§r

A block can become a grid: a set of cells with tiny pieces inside.

Each piece is a real block in miniature. Redstone, pistons and Create machines work.
tinyblocks.guide.page.2:
§lThe three items§r

Minimizer: builds tiny.

Grid Save: carries finished grids.

Shaft Connector: joins a grid to big machines.
tinyblocks.guide.page.3:
§lMinimizer§r

Hold it in your off-hand and a block in your main hand.

Click a block: a grid starts next to it, with the piece inside.

Click a grid: the piece goes in.
tinyblocks.guide.page.4:
§lPast the edge?§r

If a piece goes past a grid's edge, the next grid starts by itself, at the same size.

So you can build across several blocks.
tinyblocks.guide.page.5:
§lSize§r

Hold Z to open the board, then let go on a cell, from 1/2 to 1/16. The default is 1/7.

1/1 places normal blocks.

Shift+G switches the Minimizer off, to build normally.
tinyblocks.guide.page.6:
§lOdd or even?§r

Odd sizes have a middle cell, lined up with a big shaft.

Prefer odd sizes to join machines with the Shaft Connector.
tinyblocks.guide.page.7:
§lModes (Shift+H)§r

Normal: one piece.
Fill: the whole box.
Hollow: its six faces.
Walls: its four sides.
Plane: one layer.
Destroy: breaks a grid.
tinyblocks.guide.page.8:
§lUsing the modes§r

Click two corners. A blue outline shows the result.

Ctrl + scroll: height.
Sneak-click: cancel.

At most 8192 cells.
tinyblocks.guide.page.9:
§lDestroy mode§r

A red outline shows the grid under your crosshair.

Click: the whole grid breaks, as if you mined each piece.

A locked Minimizer only destroys grids of its size.
tinyblocks.guide.page.10:
§lLock (K)§r

Press K with the Minimizer in hand: it glows.

You then only break grids of its size. Normal blocks and other sizes are safe.
tinyblocks.guide.page.11:
§lMinimize me (X)§r

Press X with it in hand to shrink to its size.

Your reach stays the same. Press X again to go back. Leaving the world doesn't undo it.
tinyblocks.guide.page.12:
§lGrid Save§r

Keeps a whole grid in the item.

Click a grid: it leaves the world with everything inside, and nothing drops.
tinyblocks.guide.page.13:
§lPlacing it back§r

With it in hand, a ghost shows where the grid will go.

R turns it a quarter.

Click to place it. Machines and links keep working.
tinyblocks.guide.page.14:
§lCut or copy§r

Right-click the air to switch.

Cut, the default: the grid leaves the world.

Copy, creative only: the grid stays and the item keeps a copy.
tinyblocks.guide.page.15:
§lSelection mode§r

Empty, sneak-click one corner, then click the other.

Green: it can take it.
Yellow: it can't.

Up to 4 grids, 4 blocks a side. Sneak-click the air to cancel.
tinyblocks.guide.page.16:
§lWhen it refuses§r

Something in the grid is still moving, like a piston.

The grid holds too much.

When placing, the spot is taken.
tinyblocks.guide.page.17:
§lShaft Connector§r

Joins Create's rotation between the big world and a grid.

Click a piece of the grid: it goes on the nearest face. On a tiny shaft, at the end of its line.
tinyblocks.guide.page.18:
§lOdd grid: funnel§r

Its wide end meets the shaft outside. Its narrow end is a socket in the middle cell.

With a Minimizer, click it with a block: it goes in the socket, lined up.
tinyblocks.guide.page.19:
§lEven grid: gear§r

It sits against the face.

Small tiny cogwheels fit on its sides, and the mechanism runs from them.

It takes no tiny shaft.
tinyblocks.guide.page.20:
§lJoining outside§r

Without a Minimizer, click the wide end with a big shaft.

It goes outside the grid, lined up, with no support. A ghost shows where.
tinyblocks.guide.page.21:
§lMoving, removing§r

A wrench moves the connector to the next free face.

Sneak and use the wrench to take it apart.
tinyblocks.guide.page.22:
§lCreate, schematics§r

Wrenches, casings, value settings, goggles and redstone links work in a grid.

Grids go in schematics and print with their pieces. They ride vehicles too.
